questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A country far away and a country with great travel opportunities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Good overall information, but more general to all students.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Help from the law chambers and student advisers. 
Attented the orientation and any intro events.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Lacked help getting the right units.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Through online recommendations and research. Lots of student housing in the city, if you are willing to pay. I lived on a Scape campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Very expensive, but worth it to live in the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: No housing close to campus for students in the city.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very hard to pick units and make a schedule. Specifically for post-grad law.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You pick classes in advance, and make a list, but do not have a lot of information, before making the list. Please choose at least 8 units, you want to attended. Many of mine got cancelled or moved.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Students counsellors.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very, got more online classes than what was allowed on my visa, and had to change last minute, to get placed in any available units.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: As lots of questions before picking units, and don't make travelplans, before you have your final schedule.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: 4 post-grad classes at the law chambers. The level was higher than KU, but all exams were papers.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: All exams were take-home exams.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: LAW5081 - Australian legal process and research, LAW5356 - Current issues in workplace law, LAW5432 - Workplace investigations and misconduct, LAW5356 - White Collar and Corporate Crime.

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: LAW5081 - Australian legal process and research is a good overall knowledge class.

Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *

Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The visa cost AUD 2,028, and there is a mandatory health insurance (OSHC) costing AUD 334, in addition to Danish health insurance.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out is cheaper than in Denmark, but groceries can be more expensive. Gym memberships are also somewhat more expensive than in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Most non-academic opportunities are at the main campuses, so the post-grad law students are not offered many opptions in the Law Chambers.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Clubs and sports.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I was part of the Surf club and the Outdoor club, which offered trips with other students. Great opportunity to meet others, and more Australians as well.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Uluru - purchase a package, where you can sleep in swags and hike. F1 is also in Melbourne, but you have to get tickets a few months before, to get good ones.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It's a very multicultural city, so easy to adjust, and there are a lot of foreigners.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be a part of a club and talk to students in class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: A lot of asian students were used to relying more on GenAI than we are used to in Denmark, and a lot of them were not comfortable speaking English.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The multicultural approach, and you are not "different" than everyone else, because everyone is so used to foreigners.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be part of a club and tell the professors that you are from Denmark and live in the city, if you can.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware of the many different campuses. Monash campus is so far out of the city.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Travelling Australia and getting out of my comfort zone.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting the right schedule and classes to match. The time zone compared to Denmark can be hard as well.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
